subject.title: fix(sms): ack rate-limited Twilio callbacks instead of dropping them [AI]

question: Should the SMS webhook report success for a validated callback that OpenClaw intentionally discards, or require dispatch or durable queue acceptance before returning 2xx?
rationale: This chooses the channel's overload and delivery contract and affects operator retry configuration, monitoring, and compatibility; implementation mechanics alone cannot safely decide it.

options.title: Require durable acceptance
options.body: Return 2xx only after dispatch or durable enqueue succeeds, retaining a failure response when OpenClaw does not accept the callback.

options.title: Approve acknowledged drops
options.body: Intentionally return 200 for over-limit validated callbacks and accept permanent message loss without Twilio retry or failure reporting.

options.title: Retain current rejection
options.body: Keep the current HTTP 429 contract and improve retry documentation if durable buffering is outside the desired scope.

recommendation.title: Require durable acceptance
recommendation.body: Return 2xx only after dispatch or durable enqueue succeeds, retaining a failure response when OpenClaw does not accept the callback.

likelyOwner.reason: The current quota and validation ordering on main came from their merged SMS webhook work, making them the strongest available routing candidate for this contract choice.
